last_test: The recited mortgage has been located: Registry of Deeds memorial 536082, dated 16 March 1824, DGS 008091882 images 226–227. It names John Glasgow junior of Cookstown, grocer, and John Glasgow senior of Gortin, farmer. It secures junior’s £50 debt to senior and indemnifies senior for two bonds totaling £150, payable to William Glasgow, farmer in County Tyrone, and the Reverend John Harkness. Hugh Glasgow witnesses the transaction. This is the underlying mortgage recited in the 1825 assignment, not a second independent family transaction.
next_test: Identify William Glasgow, farmer and £100 bond creditor, and Hugh Glasgow, witness, in memorial 536082. Verify uncertain witness placenames before assigning a profile. Compare the existing Gortin Hugh-2540 without excluding him solely for an estimated 1805 birth. Test the 1822 Harkness mortgage and family/property succession next; the recited 1824 mortgage is located and must not be searched afresh.
conclusion: No father/son clause was found in the inspected original mortgage passages. The Gortin father hypothesis stays possible, 45%; profile identifications remain inferred. William the creditor and Hugh the witness are not securely assigned to existing profiles, and their exact locations are not asserted. The existing Gortin Hugh (Glasgow-2540, estimated birth 1805) is a compatible witness candidate by name and chronology, not an identified signatory. A younger witness is not excluded solely by that estimate. The 1825 recital and this mortgage share one underlying financial arrangement and must not be counted as independent kinship proofs. Full diplomatic transcription, uncertain witness placenames and exact jurat date remain outstanding.
